scope: Universal finite bit-word bijection; NOT device driver, not modulation, not D2 control. Core vs library minimality requires independent owner review.

history.origin: Frank Gray, Pulse Code Communication, US2632058A, filed 1947, granted 1953; IBM Johnsson/Ho 1995
history.passage: Reflected n-bit code has unique codeword per rank, every adjacent codeword differs in one bit.

owners_hobbies: FPGA Tang computing and CDC pointers

known_neighbors: D10 DIFFERENTIAL-ENCODE separately proposed, not a synonym
checks.novelty_caveat: XOR/shift projections may be composed; owner must decide if named map is an admissible D10 resident or library derivation; exact name absence is not semantic irreducibility evidence.

rows.behavior: For unsigned w-bit binary rank n (0<=n<2^w), return w-bit binary-reflected Gray codeword n XOR (n shifted right once); preserve declared width including leading zeroes.
rows.primary_formula: g = n XOR (n >> 1), restricted to width w
positive_witnesses: Adjacent and cyclic ranks have Hamming distance 1 for w>=1
falsifiers: w4 gray 7 vs gray8 changes more than one bit
drops leading zeroes or permits 16 at width4
rows.root_question: Derivable using XOR and right shift; a selected named mathematical map but not independently proven primitive.

rows.behavior: For a width w reflected Gray codeword g, recover unsigned rank n by XOR prefix from most significant Gray bit to least, preserving width.
rows.primary_formula: binary_bit[i]=XOR(gray_bit[j] for j>=i); prefix XOR modulo 2
rows.root_question: Prefix XOR expressible using general reductions; owner to decide Core vs derived library.
